fi-microdevario-kubotai.title: Kubotai Rasbora
fi-microdevario-kubotai.summary: Microdevario kubotai is a miniature cyprinid from peninsular Thailand and the Salween drainage in southern Myanmar. Relatively common in the ornamental trade, it is sold under names including 'green…
rows: schooling species typically occurring in groups of 20-50 individuals in nature, therefore the purchase of at least 8-10 is recommended.
Likely to feed on small invertebrates, algae and other zooplankton in nature.
Known from Ranong and Phang Nga provinces on the northwestern slope of peninsular Thailand and the Ataran River basin, a tributary within the Salween drainage in southern Myanmar…
notes: Looks particularly effective in a planted arrangement with a darker substrate, and can appear a little washed out in sparsely-decorated set-ups.
Also thrives in a set-up designed to resemble a flowing river or stream with a substrate of variably-sized rocks and gravel and some large water-worn boulders.

fi-trigonostigma-hengeli.title: Hengel's Rasbora
fi-trigonostigma-hengeli.summary: Trigonostigma hengeli is a small rasbora from the Greater Sunda Islands, collected in Jambi province, Sumatra and apparently West Kalimantan, Borneo. It is sometimes sold as the 'glowlight rasbora',…
rows: schooling species by nature and really should be kept in a group of at least 8-10 specimens.
Carnivore / micropredator. Probably a micropredator feeding on small insects, worms, crustaceans, and other zooplankton in nature.
Certainly restricted to the Greater Sunda Islands although the exact extent of its range is unclear.
notes: Choice of decor is not especially critical although it tends to show better colouration when maintained in a well-furnished set-up with a dark substrate, and it's a relatively popular choice for carefully-aquascaped arrangements.
A more natural-looking arrangement might consist of a soft, sandy substrate with wood roots and branches placed such a way that plenty of shady spots and caves are formed.

fi-rasbora-borapetensis.title: Brilliant Rasbora
fi-rasbora-borapetensis.summary: The red-tailed rasbora, Rasbora borapetensis, is a small cyprinid from the Mekong and Chao Phraya drainages and the Mae Klong in western Thailand. One of the more commonly encountered rasboras in…
rows: schooling species by nature and really should be kept in a group of at least 8-10 specimens.
Predator / carnivore. Stomach analyses of wild specimens have revealed it to be a micropredator feeding on small insects, worms, crustaceans and other zooplankton.
Occurs in the great Mekong and Chao Phraya river drainages as well as the Mae Klong in western Thailand.
notes: Choice of decor is not especially critical although the fish tend to show better colouration when maintained in a well-planted set-up with a dark substrate.
The addition of some floating plants and driftwood roots or branches to diffuse the light entering the tank also seems to be appreciated and adds a more natural feel.

fi-rasbora-trilineata.title: Scissortail Rasbora
fi-rasbora-trilineata.summary: The scissortail rasbora, Rasbora trilineata, is a cyprinid from the Chao Phraya and lower Mekong basins, Peninsular Malaysia, Sumatra and Borneo. The name comes from the twitching of the caudal fin…
rows: Schooling / social — keep a proper group
According to stomach analyses of wild specimens this species feeds mainly on invertebrates both aquatic and terrestrial, particularly insects.
Native to the Chao Phraya and lower Mekong river basins in Laos, Thailand and Cambodia and is widespread in Peninsular Malaysia with its distribution also extending into the…
notes: Choice of decor is not as critical as water quality and the amount of open swimming-space provided.

We suggest keeping it in a large, well-planted aquarium or alternatively it would look superb in a set-up designed to resemble a flowing river with a substrate of variably-sized rocks and gravel and some large water-worn boulders.

fi-trigonostigma-espei.title: Espei Rasbora
fi-trigonostigma-espei.summary: The lambchop rasbora, Trigonostigma espei, is a small cyprinid from southwestern and southeastern Thailand, reaching into southwestern Cambodia. It can be confused with T. heteromorpha and T. hengeli…
rows: schooling species by nature and really should be kept in a group of at least 8-10 specimens.
Predator / carnivore. Probably a micropredator feeding on small insects, worms, crustaceans, and other zooplankton in nature.
There appear to be two main populations of this species, one in the far southwest of Thailand and the other in the southeast of the country around the border with Cambodia.
notes: Choice of decor is not especially critical although it tends to show better colouration when maintained in a well-furnished set-up with a dark substrate, and it's a relatively popular choice for carefully-aquascaped arrangements.
A more natural-looking arrangement might consist of a soft, sandy substrate with wood roots and branches placed such a way that plenty of shady spots and caves are formed.
